authority: classification of the maintained nonclosed topic register; not a claim that the science is solved
admissionRule: A corpus-ready finite task must have a named carrier, all source inputs present, a bounded computation or proof, an independent verifier and a stop rule. No maintained nonclosed topic presently satisfies all five without making a new physical or mathematical choice.

groups.meaning: The model or protocol is sufficiently specified to point at an apparatus, but closure requires fabrication, calibration, measured covariance or observed records.
The next calculation is known, but the declared compute scale is not provisioned or the source artifacts needed for reproduction are not public in the corpus.
A finite calculation would be premature because the carrier, action, representation map, physical process, ultraviolet completion or cross-grade operator has not yet been selected and sourced.
The requested promotion currently requires a theorem or ultraviolet control not supplied by the programme and not honestly approximated by another finite scan.
These are maintenance disciplines rather than missing physics computations; they remain live whenever the corpus changes.

interpretation.closed: The explicit corpus search has reached a typed frontier: every maintained nonclosed topic is owned and has a reopening datum.
interpretation.notClosed: The frontier itself is not exhausted. Forty-five topics remain outside closed status, and most now require experiment, calibration, public-data execution, a new sourced construction, unavailable artifacts or a recognized theorem.
interpretation.implication: Further autonomous algebra or simulation without one of those new data would add model freedom rather than evidence. The next useful move is to acquire the named datum, not to elaborate the same abstraction.
